angle_name: Product-form Perron amortization of the hyperbola-truncated mu*Lambda bilinear form (full-constant Korobov-Vinogradov Abel bound) — ADJACENT ANGLE, marked as such: the pure Type-II prime-correlation route was assessed and honestly declined (see mechanism).
mechanism: First bridge pi to psi: R(t) = (psi(t)-t)/log t + integral term + O(sqrt(t)); summed over d <= K with absolute values this costs O(x^{3/4} log x), absorbed at KV tolerance. The core object becomes T(x) = Sum_{d<=K} mu(d)(psi(x/d) - x/d), whose double sum Sum_{dn<=x, d<=K} mu(d)Lambda(n) has Dirichlet-series kernel F_K(s)·(-zeta'/zeta)(s) with F_K(s) = Sum_{d<=K} mu(d) d^{-s}. Perron with truncation height T = exp((log x)^{3/5}) and contour shifted to sigma(t) = 1 - alpha·delta(t), where delta(t) = c0/((log(|t|+3))^{2/3}(loglog(|t|+3))^{1/3}) is the Vinogradov-Korobov zero-free width and alpha = 1 - 1/loglog x. The only pole crossed is s=1, whose residue x·F_K(1) cancels EXACTLY against the subtracted main term x·Sum_{d<=K} mu(d)/d — no Mertens-strength input needed for the main term at all. On the contour, zeta'/zeta << (log t)^{2/3}(loglog t)^{1/3} (standard in the VK region). The new step: bound F_K(sigma(t)+it) NOT trivially (K^{1-sigma}) but by an inner Perron shift of width (1-alpha)delta(t) that stays inside the zero-free region, giving F_K << K^{-(1-alpha)delta(t)} polylog — genuine mu-cancellation at every height t, obtained without ever separating F_K from the prime factor or entering the critical strip. Multiplying the two savings in the integrand yields x^{sigma}·K^{-(1-alpha)delta} = x·exp(-delta(t)·log x·(1+alpha)/2) -> x·exp(-delta·log x) as alpha -> 1, i.e., the FULL KV constant at argument x, versus the halved constant (log(sqrt x))^{3/5} that the triangle inequality is forced into by its smallest sample. This is the concrete demonstration that keeping the mu x prime-phase interaction alive as a product (rather than splitting by triangle/Cauchy-Schwarz over d) buys a measurable, provable improvement over the honest trivial bound. The pure assigned lens (Vaughan Type-II + Cauchy-Schwarz opening R(x/mn)R(x/mn') prime correlations at multiplicative shifts n/n') was worked and declined: its off-diagonal correlations are unconditionally equivalent to zero pair-correlation inputs, which do not exist at any power saving, and the Cauchy-Schwarz step both discards the mu signs and re-enters expansion territory. Ceiling statement, plainly: mu enters linearly, so KV/PNT strength is the parity-permitted maximum for this machinery; no unconditional power saving (rung 1 in exponent form) and no rung 2 are reachable by this angle.
new_leverage: Three items, all UNVERIFIED speculation until computed. (1) Product-form contour: the mu-polynomial F_K(s) and the prime kernel -zeta'/zeta(s) are bounded jointly inside one integrand, so their cancellations MULTIPLY — exp(-delta·alpha·log x)·exp(-delta·(1-alpha)·log K) — instead of the triangle inequality's minimum-sample bottleneck; this recovers the full KV constant c0(log x)^{3/5} versus the trivial-bound constant c0·2^{-3/5}(log x)^{3/5}, a strict factor-1.516 exponent improvement over the honest trivial bound. (2) Exact residue cancellation: the s=1 residue x·F_K(1) cancels identically against the subtracted main term, so no Mertens/M(d)^2 input appears anywhere — the argument is structurally outside the F-closure class by input inventory, not by assertion. (3) Everything is pointwise in x (Perron at the pinned point), so the pinned-vs-averaged obstacle is void by construction; the same machinery applies verbatim to the boundary term M(K)R(y) via the Dirichlet polynomial pairing at argument y.
target_estimate: Theorem A (full-constant KV Abel bound), unconditional. Let y ≍ sqrt(x), K = floor(x/(y+1)). For every eps > 0 there is x0 such that for all x >= x0: |Sum_{d<=K} mu(d)·R(floor(x/d))| <= C·x·exp(-(1-eps)·c0·(log x)^{3/5}(log log x)^{-1/5}), where c0 is the Korobov-Vinogradov constant in psi(x)-x << x·exp(-c0(log x)^{3/5}(loglog x)^{-1/5}). Variables and ranges: Perron height T = exp((log x)^{3/5}); contour sigma(t) = 1 - alpha·delta(t), delta(t) = c0/((log(|t|+3))^{2/3}(loglog(|t|+3))^{1/3}), alpha = 1 - 1/loglog x; inner Perron shift width (1-alpha)delta(t) for the F_K bound, valid for all |t| <= T. Itemized losses: pi-psi bridge << x^{3/4} log x (absolute values, absorbed); Perron truncation << x log^2 x / T; residue at s=1: exactly 0 after cancellation with -x·F_K(1); contour integral << x·(log T)^{O(1)}·exp(-delta(T)·log x·(1+alpha)/2); F_K-lemma polylog losses (log T)^{O(1)}. Baseline it must beat (my derived honest trivial bound): triangle + pointwise KV-PNT gives <= x·exp(-c0·2^{-3/5}(1-eps)(log x)^{3/5}(loglog x)^{-1/5}); Theorem A improves the exponent constant by the factor 2^{3/5} ≈ 1.516.

obstacle_positions.F_closure: Exits the class by input inventory, not assertion: no Sum M(d)^2 Mertens-energy input appears anywhere (the s=1 residue cancels the main term exactly, so even Sum mu(d)/d is never estimated). Recombination is a single contour integral in which F_K(s) and -zeta'/zeta(s) stay multiplied; no Cauchy-Schwarz/Hoelder/triangle split over d occurs before both cancellations are extracted. The mu x prime sign interaction is retained as the product F_K(s)·zeta'/zeta(s) in the integrand. Honest caveat: the final t-integral IS bounded by absolute values, which is precisely why the method caps at KV strength.
obstacle_positions.fiber_growth: Not triggered. No pair-to-modulus transfer, no shared reduced denominators, no conductors: the only 'off-diagonal' objects in the declined pure-Type-II variant were zero pairs, and the committed angle never opens them. Coordinates are (sigma, t) on one contour, not (d, d', a, a').
obstacle_positions.pinned_vs_averaged: Void by construction — a genuine merit of this angle. Perron is evaluated at the pinned x; the zero-free region, the zeta'/zeta bound, and the F_K inner-Perron lemma are all pointwise-in-t statements holding for every x. No L^2 average over translates, no exceptional set anywhere.
obstacle_positions.modulus_magnitude: Bypassed. No wheel modulus enters; the only 'conductor-like' scale is the Perron height T = exp((log x)^{3/5}), which is subpolynomial. The obstacle is about a different coordinate system that this angle never uses.
obstacle_positions.parity: Fully conceded and load-bearing. mu enters linearly; the parity wall is exactly why the ceiling of this angle is KV/PNT strength and why I claim no unconditional power saving. The angle is calibrated to extract the maximum the parity barrier permits (full KV constant) rather than pretend to cross it.
obstacle_positions.circularity: Clean. The d=1 term R(x) is bounded by unconditional KV-PNT inside the same contour argument; no RH-strength pointwise bound is used anywhere, conditionally or inductively. The target's RH-equivalence is untouched: this angle is strictly a rung-0/0.5 unconditional contribution.
obstacle_positions.finite_range: The 0.35-0.43 calibration constant plays no role in any claim; all statements are asymptotic and unconditional. Numerics are used only in the kill test to falsify (checking S stays under the claimed envelope shape at x <= 10^9), never to support.

kill_test: One day, three parts, cheapest first. (a) Literature kill (2 hours): check Ivic ch. 1/12, Ramachandra, and twisted-Moebius-sum literature for (i) an existing bound on the hyperbola-truncated sum Sum_{d<=sqrt x} mu(d)(psi(x/d)-x/d) and (ii) the inner-Perron lemma F_K(sigma+it) << K^{-(1-alpha)delta(t)} polylog on the VK boundary — if (i) exists the deliverable is dead as novel; if a counterexample-shaped obstruction to (ii) exists (the w-shift truncation reintroducing K^{+} terms) Theorem A degrades to the trivial-constant version. (b) The load-bearing computation (half day): write out the inner Perron shift for F_K(sigma(t)+it) with explicit w-truncation bookkeeping, uniformly in |t| <= T; the single most likely failure point is that the w-contour cannot shift left of Re w = -(1-alpha)delta(t) without zeta(s+w) losing its zero-free guarantee at heights near t, and that the truncation error K^{c}/T' swamps the K^{-(1-alpha)delta} gain. If the bookkeeping fails, the angle collapses to the triangle-equivalent constant and is not worth writing. (c) Numerical falsifier (2 hours, existing data <= 10^9): compute S(x) at x in {10^6..10^9} against the envelope x·exp(-c(log x)^{3/5}) with fitted c; the test kills if S trends toward a missed main term (S/envelope tending to a nonzero constant), which would indicate an error in the residue-cancellation or the pi-psi bridge accounting.
rung0_plan: Stage 1 (one week, classical machinery only): prove the alpha=0 version — Perron with trivial F_K bound K^{1-sigma}/(1-sigma) on the VK contour, exact residue cancellation at s=1, pi-psi bridge at x^{3/4} tolerance — yielding S << x·exp(-c(log x)^{3/5}(loglog x)^{-1/5}) unconditionally. Honest disclosure: this shape is ALSO reachable by triangle inequality plus pointwise KV-PNT (with constant halved through log sqrt(x)), so Stage 1 alone is a machinery-establishing entrant, not new strength; the packet's rung 0 as literally stated (any unconditional PNT-strength bound, o of trivial scale) is satisfied but I flag that it may be considered trivially satisfiable and the project should recalibrate rung 0 to 'beat the triangle-KV constant'. Stage 2 (the actual deliverable, 1-2 additional weeks): the inner-Perron F_K cancellation lemma and the alpha -> 1 optimization, giving Theorem A with the full constant — the first statement about this Abel sum strictly better than its honest trivial bound. Formalization note (UNVERIFIED): a Lean version would need a zero-free region with explicit error; if mathlib/PrimeNumberTheoremAnd machinery only supports the classical de la Vallee Poussin region, the formalizable variant is S << x·exp(-c·sqrt(log x)), same proof skeleton.
plausible_partial: Named: 'Full-constant KV Abel bound' (Theorem A above) — unconditional |Sum_{d<=K} mu(d) R(floor(x/d))| << x·exp(-(1-eps)c0(log x)^{3/5}(loglog x)^{-1/5}) with the full KV constant c0, strictly beating the honest triangle baseline by the factor 2^{3/5} in the exponent constant; provable at bounded effort (2-3 weeks) conditional only on the inner-Perron F_K lemma surviving the kill test's bookkeeping. Fallback partial if the F_K lemma dies: Theorem A0, the triangle-constant version via the product contour, still valuable as the pinned, exceptional-set-free, F-closure-exempt derivation with exact main-term cancellation, plus its de la Vallee Poussin variant S << x·exp(-c·sqrt(log x)) as the realistically Lean-formalizable statement.
self_assessed_risk: Weakest assumption, stated plainly: that the inner Perron shift bounding F_K(sigma(t)+it) with genuine mu-cancellation ON the shifted contour survives explicit truncation bookkeeping — I have not done the w-truncation arithmetic, and evaluation points inside the strip are exactly where 1/zeta representations become singular; this is the single hinge of the non-trivial claim. Probabilities (all UNVERIFIED speculation): some KV-strength bound on the Abel sum survives write-up ~90% (it already follows from triangle + KV-PNT, which is also why its novelty is low); Theorem A with the full constant survives ~55-65%; the project or literature already knows an equivalent hyperbola-truncated result ~25-35%. Hard honesty items: this lens cannot touch rung 2; no unconditional power saving is reachable (parity ceiling); the assigned lens's centerpiece (bilinear Cauchy-Schwarz with prime correlations at multiplicative shifts) was evaluated and is unworkable without zero pair-correlation inputs, so my committed angle is adjacent-defensible, not the pure lens; and the deliverable's improvement over trivial is a constant factor in the exponent, not an exponent change — modest, but it is the precise, provable cash value of keeping the mu x R sign interaction alive as the packet demands.
